# The DexNav

The DexNav of Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire, in all three versions. It sits on the touch screen while you explore (the screen that used to stay empty) and has a page in the PokéNav. It shows the wild Pokémon of the place you are in, and it finds hidden Pokémon for you: they can come with perfect IVs, an egg move, their hidden ability or a rare held item, and now and then a shiny one.

## Getting it

Prof. Birch gives you the DexNav in his Lab, together with the Pokédex, right after your rival gives you Poké Balls. The touch screen turns into the DexNav at once.

Already playing? If your save has its Pokédex from an older version, talk to Prof. Birch in his Lab and he gives you the DexNav, before anything else he has for you.

## The tutorial on Route 101

The first time you step into the tall grass of Route 101 after getting it, your rival (May, or Brendan if you play as May) runs up and shows you how it works:

- If you have no Poké Balls left, your rival gives you 2.
- The DexNav finds a Poochyena hiding in shaking grass a few steps away. It knows Thunder Fang, Ice Fang or Fire Fang, one of its egg moves.
- Walk onto the shaking grass to battle it. It is a normal wild battle: catch it or knock it out. This one doesn't run off if you hurry.
- Afterwards your rival says goodbye and leaves. If you leave Route 101 before the battle, the shaking grass is back the next time you walk there.

## The screen

**The area map.** A map of the place you are in, drawn with its Gen 3 tiles. Each of its wild Pokémon stands on a tile of the kind it lives on: the ones of the tall grass, cave floor or sand on the ground, the ones you meet while surfing on the water. A Pokémon you have caught is in colour, one you have only seen is a dark shape, and one you haven't seen is a "?". A crown appears when you have caught every Pokémon of the place, and tapping the map tells you how far you are ("There are Pokémon here you haven't caught yet!", "Almost done! Just a few left to catch here!", "Well done! You've caught every Pokémon here!"). A place without wild Pokémon shows "No wild Pokémon live here." The POKéNAV button opens the PokéNav, once you have it.

The DexNav lists the Pokémon of the tall grass, cave floors, sand and water. Pokémon you fish, find with Rock Smash or meet roaming, and Feebas, aren't on it. After the Champion it shows the area's new Pokémon too (completing the Pokédex: [Sapphire](postgame-sapphire.md#completing-the-pokédex), [Ruby](postgame-ruby.md#completing-the-pokédex), [Emerald](postgame-emerald.md#completing-the-pokédex)).

**Found Pokémon.** Tap a Pokémon you have seen: its picture, name, type and search level, and SEARCH. (One you haven't seen: "You haven't seen this Pokémon yet.")

**Hidden Pokémon.** While a Pokémon hides, this shows what the DexNav knows about it. Its level always; the rest only from a high enough search level for that species (before that it shows "???"):

| Shown | From search level |
|---|---|
| Level | always |
| Potential: a gold star for each perfect IV (up to three) | 5 |
| Ability ("!" for its hidden ability) | 10 |
| First Move ("!" for an egg move) | 25 |

The bonuses are decided when the search starts, so the battle's Pokémon is the one the screen shows.

## Searching

1. Tap a Pokémon on the area map, then SEARCH. Pokémon of the ground need you on foot; for one of the water you must be surfing ("Go surfing to look for this one.").
2. The DexNav hides it 3 to 5 steps away (2 when there is no room further out), in a spot you can walk (or surf) to: shaking tall grass, a dust cloud on a cave floor or in the desert sand, or rippling water. "It's hiding nearby! Sneak up on it." When there is nowhere to put it: "Nothing could be found here."
3. Walk onto the spot: a wild battle with that Pokémon starts, with the normal wild battle music. Catch it or knock it out.

- While it hides, no other wild Pokémon jump out at you.
- If you leave the area, or someone walks onto the spot, it is gone ("It got away...").
- The DexNav also works as a page of the PokéNav: its DEXNAV button. There the D-pad moves a cursor over the Pokémon and A picks one; starting a search closes the PokéNav.

## Sneaking

Walk to it. If you run (holding B) or ride your Bicycle within 3 steps of the spot, the Pokémon runs off ("It ran off! Move more slowly.") and your chain ends.

## Search levels

Every species has its own search level. It goes up by 1 each time you catch or knock out a Pokémon of that species found with the DexNav (the tutorial's counts too), up to 255. The Found and Hidden screens show it. A higher search level shows more on the Hidden screen ([above](#the-screen)) and gives better bonuses. Saves from older versions start every species at 0.

## Bonuses

Each Pokémon the DexNav finds can get these, by the search level of its species:

| Search level | Perfect IVs | Hidden ability | Egg move | Rare held item |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-4 | 10% chance of 1 | 0% | 20% | 5% |
| 5-9 | 1 | 5% | 30% | 10% |
| 10-24 | 1, 20% chance of 2 | 10% | 40% | 15% |
| 25-49 | 2 | 15% | 50% | 20% |
| 50-99 | 2, 30% chance of 3 | 20% | 60% | 25% |
| 100-255 | 3 | 25% | 60% | 25% |

- **Perfect IVs:** that many of its six stats get the highest IV, 31 (different stats, at random).
- **Hidden ability:** its hidden ability (from Black 2's data), only for a Pokémon whose hidden ability differs from its usual ones. Otherwise it has one of its usual abilities.
- **Egg move:** one of its egg moves (for an evolved Pokémon, its first stage's), in its first empty move slot, or in place of its first move.
- **Rare held item:** it holds its rarer wild item, the one wild Pokémon of its kind hold 5% of the time (only Pokémon that have one).

## Chains and shiny Pokémon

Your chain goes up by 1 each time you catch or knock out a DexNav Pokémon of the same species as the last one (up to 999). It goes back to 0 when you search for another species, when the Pokémon runs off or its spot is lost, and when you run from the battle or lose it. The DexNav doesn't show the chain: count it yourself.

Every wild Pokémon has a 1 in 8,192 chance to be shiny. A DexNav Pokémon gets extra tries at that chance: one for every 5 in your chain (10 from a chain of 50 on), one for every 50 search levels of its species, and 20 more when your chain is exactly 50 or 100. Some examples:

| Chain | Search level 0 | Search level 50 | Search level 100 | Search level 255 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1 in 8,192 | 1 in 4,096 | 1 in 2,731 | 1 in 1,366 |
| 5 | 1 in 4,096 | 1 in 2,731 | 1 in 2,048 | 1 in 1,171 |
| 25 | 1 in 1,366 | 1 in 1,171 | 1 in 1,024 | 1 in 745 |
| 49 | 1 in 820 | 1 in 745 | 1 in 683 | 1 in 547 |
| 50 | 1 in 265 | 1 in 256 | 1 in 249 | 1 in 228 |
| 51 | 1 in 745 | 1 in 683 | 1 in 631 | 1 in 512 |
| 100 | 1 in 265 | 1 in 256 | 1 in 249 | 1 in 228 |

## Good to know

- It works with saves from older versions: talk to Prof. Birch to get it ([above](#getting-it)).
- In the Safari Zone a search costs only the steps you walk, and the Pokémon it finds follow the Safari Zone's rules ([Sapphire](wild-pokemon-sapphire.md#safari-zone-rules), [Ruby](wild-pokemon-ruby.md#safari-zone-rules), [Emerald](wild-pokemon-emerald.md#safari-zone-rules)).
- Searching never changes the normal wild Pokémon: walking in the grass without a search is as before, and the [wild Pokémon pages](README.md) show the same tables.
